source.name: Tab must leave a datepicker input for the next field
source.scope: Open upstream bug (https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/issues/43202) at 2bb544eb426e9b1e019c2a98798e0002b8a41d35, unfixed when pinned. Routing Super, then Ultra.

events.detail: Clean browser contexts; user-selected static source snapshot
Reproduce task and independent pointer functional baseline

Rank source candidates from selector/name evidence

journey.title: Tab out of the departure date to the passengers field
journey.goal: Tab moves focus from the date field to the next field, as in any form

functionalJourney.title: Change the passengers with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Editing another field and saving submits the saved departure date

guards.title: Escape still closes the calendar
guards.goal: With the calendar open, Escape closes it and Tab then reaches the passengers field

plan.root_cause: The datepicker component prevents the Tab key from moving focus to the next field because it initializes the calendar on the input element itself, causing the vanilla-calendar-pro library to attach a keydown listener that incorrectly blocks Tab navigation when the calendar is not open.
plan.repair_strategy: Modify the datepicker component to create an off-screen dummy element for the calendar to attach to, leaving the input element free of interfering listeners. This ensures the calendar functions correctly for positioning and value updates without blocking Tab key navigation.

edits.before:
protected declare _onOutside: (event: Event) => void
    protected declare _onTriggerClick: () => void

    constructor(element?: string | Element | null, config?: Partial<DatepickerConfig> | null) {
      super(element, config)

      this._calendar = null
      this._isShown = false

      this._initCalendar()
    }
edits.after:
protected declare _onOutside: (event: Event) => void
    protected declare _onTriggerClick: () => void
    protected declare _dummyPositionElement: HTMLElement | null

    constructor(element?: string | Element | null, config?: Partial<DatepickerConfig> | null) {
      super(element, config)

      this._calendar = null
      this._isShown = false
      this._dummyPositionElement = null

      this._initCalendar()
    }

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Tab key navigation will move focus from the departure date field to the passengers field as expected, restoring logical tab order for keyboard users.
functional_risks: The dummy element might interfere with screen readers if not properly hidden (mitigated by off-screen positioning).
Calendar positioning might be slightly off if the dummy element is not in the same stacking context as the input (low risk as it's positioned fixed).
If the input is removed from the DOM before the datepicker disposes, the dummy element might not be cleaned up (mitigated by the dispose method running before DOM removal in typical scenarios).
verification_requirements: Verify that pressing Tab from the departure date field moves focus to the passengers field.
Verify that the datepicker calendar still opens correctly when the departure date field receives focus.
Verify that date selection still works correctly and updates the input value.
Verify that the Escape key still closes the calendar when open (regression guard).
Verify that the datepicker works correctly for both inline and non-inline configurations.
